keyFindings.description: Security[authz]: the nine accountAuth routes verify the caller's token before any rate limit, so an unauthenticated flood of forged tokens naming an unknown kid makes go-oidc fetch the cluster issuer's JWKS once per request. The shared bearer they replaced needed no network, and the broker's own token-login route limits by address before verifying for exactly this reason (api/limits.go:13-21). The introspection bucket runs inside the handler, after authentication.

The Change bullet's 'While both generations fix the same name, one of their two entries holds it and every other principal is refused it' is false when the name is still held by a third principal from an earlier re-point that neither entry has since exchanged over, which the tester found. Add the one qualifying clause the architect described, since a body cannot be amended after the merge.

fastFollow: Broker exchange tidy-up: the 'UI-bearer' wording and brokertest's UIToken name; one session type for every grant instead of DefaultSession beside ExchangeSession with cross-decoding; one ServiceAccount validity check shared by accountCaller and machine.Service.VerifyServiceToken; run decide once after NewAccessRequest; move TestAFixedSessionNameAcrossARollout and its helpers into a file of its own.
